### HIG-ACCESSIBILITY-005 · Complete primary tasks with different input methods

| Field | Rule and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | apple_guidance |
| Phases | layout_analysis, adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype |
| Applies when | When the prototype includes interaction and input flows. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Adaptation must consider input methods and their accessibility. HTML implements equivalent interactions that the browser can verify. |
| Workspace action | Define input, reading, actions and outcomes around the current app's primary tasks. Manage text-input/IME focus, keyboard-navigation focus and assistive-reading focus separately. Record their initial positions, order, visibility, fallback when a pane change removes a target, and entry/return targets for overlays. HTML implements browser-verifiable equivalents; native acceptance records VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access. |
| Verification method | Use keyboard and available browser assistive technology to complete primary tasks, enter and close overlays, and collapse panes during a task. Verify visible outcomes and each focus type separately. Use target-iOS VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access for independent native acceptance only during native implementation; browser keyboard operation or input focus cannot substitute for assistive-reading focus or native evidence. |

| Kind | product_choice |
| Phases | adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype |

| Phases | layout_analysis, adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype, native_implementation |
| Applies when | When the target interface is rendered by SwiftUI or UIKit, including Swift and Objective-C. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Read current view/window dimensions or SwiftUI GeometryReader/onGeometryChange and refresh on size changes. Do not choose layout from UIScreen.main, startup caches, device orientation, userInterfaceIdiom or known-model size tables. Read scale from traitCollection.displayScale or the displayScale environment, and create windows through scenes. Handle all safe-area edges separately. System containers avoid reserved regions; custom layouts query them when needed. SwiftUI uses GeometryProxy.reservedRegions with occlusion versus division; UIKit uses UIView.reservedRegions. Frames use queried-view coordinates in points and include margins. A division is active only while partially folded. Consult target-SDK documentation; HTML only simulates labeled assumptions. |
| Workspace action | Identify main-screen dimensions, orientation/idiom conditions and custom-component region needs in the layout matrix. Design.md and HTML use current-container dimensions; native implementation records queried views, kind, activity and coordinates. Apply the exported Apple Skill to Swift/Objective-C migration under NATIVE-RESIZABILITY-001; otherwise retain the export gap. |
| Verification method | Check narrow, wide, low-height and threshold sizes to ensure layout no longer follows orientation/model tables. During native work, use the target SDK to check that reservedRegions includes only intersecting regions and margins are not added twice. HTML success does not establish API operation in the actual project. |

| Applies when | When the visible interface is HTML/CSS in WKWebView, including Capacitor, Cordova, Ionic, uni-app, Taro or a custom shell. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Use current visual-viewport/container dimensions rather than startup screen.width caches or one-time system-info calls. Use env(safe-area-inset-*) for the four edges only when viewport-fit=cover is effective. Keyboard, status-bar and native shell safe areas form another layer; page CSS and native handling must not pad the same edge twice. CSS receives no iOS reserved region without a verified bridge delivering it. Check native shell portions under the UIKit contract. |
| Workspace action | Record viewport configuration, safe-area CSS, width caches, keyboard/status-bar plugins and boundaries between shell and page projects. Implement page layout directly in HTML; label native shell regions as assumptions or separate gaps. |
| Verification method | Check narrow, wide, low-height and keyboard states for page-wide horizontal overflow or duplicated top/bottom spacing. Without bridge data, folded regions remain unverified. Record browser-page and WKWebView-host results separately. |
| Source IDs | MDN-ENV, MDN-VIEWPORT, SKILL-WEBVIEW, APPLE-DUO-PREPARE |

### WORKFLOW-BUILDER-001 · Prefer BUILD WEB APPS for the HTML-prototype stage

| Field | Rule and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | workflow_constraint |
| Phases | html_prototype |

| Rule / guidance / recommendation | After whole-app layout analysis and adaptation recommendations, prefer the actual BUILD WEB APPS workflow to implement the agreed prototype. It consumes the established app evidence, design and coverage contract. This is collection policy, not an Apple requirement; it does not imply that the builder is installed or that a build passes Duo acceptance. |
| Workspace action | Discover and read the real builder Skill, record its source/version/path/hash and pass the frozen baseline, recommendations, Design.md, rule/project-convention IDs, page/state coverage and continuity requirements. Preserve the current app's identity and complete all scoped tasks. Deliver editable source, runnable HTML/assets and browser/visual evidence. Installation, account setup and deployment are separate scopes; use local-only work for prototype delivery. If the actual builder cannot be obtained, record that boundary and use an equivalent available local workflow without claiming BUILD WEB APPS executed. Choose the actual existing-design refinement/testing route for minimal migration, using original App captures and components as the primary reference. Use the creation/concept route only when a new visual surface is within scope; supplementary generated concepts cannot silently replace the original design authority. |
| Verification method | Check recorded builder identity and actual execution against the handoff. Open the final artifact in a real browser, walk all scoped pages and primary tasks, exercise continuous resizing/input/overlays and inspect final screenshots. Record failures, repairs and remaining gaps separately. A plugin name, successful build or deployment alone does not establish prototype completeness or visual quality. |

### WORKFLOW-MINIMAL-001 · Migrate the whole app with the smallest necessary design changes

| Field | Rule and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | workflow_constraint |
| Phases | layout_analysis, adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype |
| Applies when | Adapting an existing app unless the user explicitly authorizes a broader redesign. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Treat actual original-app screens, shared components, tokens, content and behavior as the design authority. Preserve a working structure and use the smallest change that resolves an evidenced size, inset, reachability, continuity or accessibility problem. This is the collection's migration policy and the user's default intent, not an Apple-mandated visual style. |
| Workspace action | Extract the original visual/component baseline and classify each affected element as retain, necessary adaptation or separately optional change. Record exact before/after behavior, reason, source and affected pages. Keep the original page stack when usable; extra width alone does not require split view, new icons, new controls, rewritten copy, restyling or business changes. Match original and adapted screenshots at the same page/state/viewport, with justified exceptions. |
| Verification method | Inspect actual original/adapted image pairs and code-native shared tokens/components. Verify every in-scope page and task still works across applicable environments, each visual/behavioral difference has a reason, and optional enhancements were not promoted to required migration. |

### WORKFLOW-POSES-001 · Expose named Duo environments in one stateful review prototype

| Field | Rule and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | workflow_constraint |
| Phases | layout_analysis, adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype |
| Applies when | A default Duo adaptation prototype or an explicitly requested multi-form review is in scope. Respect documented app orientation/platform exceptions. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Show applicable outer-display orientations, inner portrait/landscape, side-by-side app-left/app-right contexts and partial-fold book/tabletop/standing examples through external review controls. Keyboard, text scaling, dialogs and overlays are stress states, not physical poses. This review contract is collection policy; it does not require a separate product design for each pose or certify native behavior. |
| Workspace action | Maintain a source-backed pose/context matrix with status, review viewport, size-class assumptions, bar edge/axis, optional active-region data and native unknowns. Numeric review dimensions and configured curve rectangles are explicitly assumptions unless measured or officially sourced; do not invent hardware sizes, camera regions or a universal center hinge. Keep one persistent running App instance and shared state; actual local viewport/container changes drive reflow. Preserve original components and container ownership; text/compound controls and keyboard accessories retain applicable exceptions. |
| Verification method | Select every applicable named context and inspect actual viewport/container dimensions, navigation edge/axis, primary actions, input/overlay ownership and no global overflow. Switch modes during editing/reading and verify route, selection, draft/selection and semantic anchor continuity. Test configured region updates, inactive/absent data and unsupported capabilities honestly. Save same-page/state original/adapted comparisons; ordinary browser resize or a decorative device frame alone does not prove multi-pose or native acceptance. |
| Source IDs | SKILL-MIGRATION-CONTRACT, SKILL-HTML-CONTRACT, APPLE-DUO-DESIGN-TALK, APPLE-DUO-BARS-TALK, APPLE-HIG-DUO |

### WORKFLOW-DEVICE-001 · Match the actual device exterior and calibrated display geometry

| Field | Rule and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | workflow_constraint |
| Phases | layout_analysis, adaptation_recommendations, html_prototype |
| Applies when | A Duo prototype includes device presentation, especially when actual Device Hub, simulator or official device appearance and dimensions are requested. |
| Rule / guidance / recommendation | Use identified actual device references and independently sourced display geometry for the shell, screen aperture, visible cutouts/buttons and supported posture views. Separate Closed, PartiallyOpen and Open physical states from orientation and app-window arrangements. Preserve original app design inside a device-focused review surface with secondary diagnostics. This is prototype-presentation policy, not an Apple hardware specification or native acceptance claim. |
| Workspace action | Record source identities and hashes, posture/orientation, display raster/logical size and scale, measured exterior/aperture landmarks, capture zoom/perspective, CSS mapping and uncertainty in the frozen design handoff. Use actual assets or reference-measured shell geometry; keep unsupported views pending and label assumptions. Apply magnification to shell and app together without changing the logical app viewport. Maintain shared task state and current comparison views; put diagnostics, raw geometry and stress controls in a collapsed inspector. |
| Verification method | Compare actual final device crops/landmarks against the identified reference, verify live app viewport dimensions and state across posture/rotation, and review shell fidelity, original-app adaptation, interaction and review usability independently. Functional counts or decorative silhouettes alone cannot establish real-device matching; retain unresolved calibration and native/hardware gaps explicitly. |
| Source IDs | SKILL-DEVICE-PRESENTATION, SKILL-MIGRATION-CONTRACT, SKILL-HTML-CONTRACT, SKILL-VALIDATION-CONTRACT |
| Status | pending |
| Adaptation decision |  |
| Reason / gap | Collection instruction materialization only. Target app and device presentation verification belong to their identified workspace and evidence. |
